**Tafsir of Surat al-Nasr (The Chapter of Help)**

It is Medinan by consensus.

Allah the Mighty and Majestic says:

﴿When the help of Allah and the conquest come,﴾ ﴿and you see people entering the religion of Allah in multitudes,﴾ ﴿then glorify your Lord with His praise and seek His forgiveness. Indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance.﴾

Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him and his father) recited: "When the help of Allah and the conquest come." 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) asked a group of the elder Companions, with Ibn 'Abbas present, about the meaning and occasion of this surah. They all said: "The apparent meaning of its wording is that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), at the conquests that were granted to him, Makkah and others, was commanded to glorify his Lord, praise Him, and seek His forgiveness." He said to Ibn 'Abbas: "What do you say, O Ibn 'Abbas?" He replied: "It is the announcement of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), which Allah the Exalted informed him of, that his time is near when he sees these things." 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "I know nothing of it except what you have mentioned."

This interpretation mentioned by Ibn 'Abbas was also mentioned by Ibn Mas'ud and his companions, Mujahid and his companions, and Qatadah and al-Dahhak. 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her) related its meaning from the Prophet (upon him be blessings and peace): "When Makkah was conquered and the Arabs embraced Islam, he (ﷺ) began to say very often: 'Glory be to Allah and by His praise, O Allah, I seek Your forgiveness,' interpreting the Qur'an in this surah. He once said: 'I think it is nothing but the approach of my appointed time.'" 'Umar and al-'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them) interpreted it in the presence of the Prophet (ﷺ), and he confirmed what they said.

The "help" that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw was his victory over Quraysh, Hawazin and others. The "conquest" is the conquest of Makkah, al-Ta'if, the cities of the Hijaz, and much of Yemen. "People entering the religion of Allah in multitudes" occurred from the conquest of Makkah until the death of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Abu 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Barr (may Allah have mercy on him) said in his book *al-Isti'ab fi Ma'rifat al-Ashab*, in the chapter on Abu Khirash al-Hudhali: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not die while there was a disbelieving man among the Arabs. Rather, after Hunayn and al-Ta'if, all of them entered Islam, some by coming in person and some by sending their delegations. Then after him (ﷺ) there was the apostasy that occurred, but they all returned to the religion."

The author (al-Qadi Abu Muhammad, may Allah have mercy on him) said:

"What is meant, Allah knows best, is the Arabs who worshipped idols. As for the Christians of Banu Taghlib, I do not think they ever embraced Islam during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), but they paid the jizyah (poll tax)."

"Afwaj" (multitudes) means groups following one group, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Into it will be thrown a company﴾ [al-Mulk: 8]. Muqatil said: what is meant by "people" is the people of Yemen, from whom seven hundred men came as a delegation. 'Ikrimah said the same. The majority said: what is meant is all the delegations of the Arabs, because they said: "Since Makkah has been conquered for Muhammad, and Allah has protected him from Abyssinia and others, there is no point in opposing him."

Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah mentioned the group of Companions and wept, and said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'People entered the religion in multitudes, and they will leave it in multitudes.'"

The Exalted's saying ﴿Indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance﴾ immediately after "and seek His forgiveness" is a great encouragement for those who seek forgiveness, may Allah make us among them. Al-Naqqash related from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him and his father) that the "help" is the Treaty of al-Hudaybiyyah, and the "conquest" is the conquest of Makkah. Ibn 'Umar said: this surah was revealed to the Prophet (ﷺ) at Mina in the middle of the Days of Tashriq, during the Farewell Pilgrimage, and he lived after it for eighty days or so.

Here ends the tafsir of Surat al-Nasr, and all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
